**Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk** is a local healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] in Denmark. It serves as a key organizational unit for monitoring and improving the quality of cardiovascular care, specifically in the treatment and management of [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation). The cluster's performance is regularly evaluated in the national quality reports published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute.

A primary measure of the cluster's clinical effectiveness is its adherence to national guidelines for anticoagulation therapy. Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk is notable for being one of the health clusters that successfully met the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation treatment for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a compliance rate of 90.8% [^src1]. 

Beyond initial treatment metrics, the cluster is tracked across a wide array of clinical quality indicators over multiple reporting periods. In the 2024 annual report, these metrics encompassed 1-year and 2-year treatment coverage [^src2], annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOACs [^src4], and the incidence of severe bleeding and heart failure within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6], [^src7]. Furthermore, Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk is included in national geographic distributions mapping the incidence of stroke (apopleksi) among atrial fibrillation patients. In these analyses, it is evaluated alongside other regional and national clusters—such as [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]], [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]], [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]], and [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]]—to identify local variations in clinical practice and patient outcomes across the Danish healthcare system [^src4].

Subsequent reporting in 2025 continues to evaluate the cluster's performance across a broad spectrum of care, including the implementation of structured patient education [^src9], waiting times for anticoagulation treatment and incidence of intracranial bleeding [^src10], and overall mortality rates among prevalent patients [^src11].
